speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: I am going to say a thing plainly, and you are going to answer it plainly, or not at all. I am tired of bargains that fit in a kitchen and break in a lane.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: You will not promise me a journey until the journey is arranged. Not a hope of a journey. Not a letter that says you meant to come. Arranged. A day, a horse or a pair of feet, a man who is actually on the road.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The eighteenth is arranged. The carrier, the bridge, the horses' pace. I walk. I carry the pack, the sheets and the inkhorn. That one I will keep, because it is set. I will not promise you another on the strength of being sorry I am on a floor.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: Good. That is the first half, and it is the half you like, because it is a date. The second half is mine. I will tell you what cannot wait. I will not wrap it in a mood and make you guess.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: You have not looked. You have a sum you will not spend in talk, and a word you have said since Susanna was in a biggin, and you have not stood in front of a house in this town and seen it as a house. Not as a speech about a house. When you can walk as far as a door, you will look. I will take you. I am not telling you which, and I am not telling you a price.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I will look. I will not buy with my mouth while I cannot stand. And I will not promise the looking has an end, until I have done it.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: That is enough of an end for a Friday. Don't promise me a house, Will. Look at one, when I show it you. Buy one, when you can. I will believe the second.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I hear you. No journey but the one that is set. No house from a floor.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: Lie still. The rest of the day can be the ceiling. I have said the part that could not wait, and I am not going to decorate it.
